Convening map

Three pilot proposals

Quick readMore contextTechnical detailSpeaker notes
  • Point to an existing pathway. If a program already serves independent contributors well, say which one and how someone gets in.
  • Offer technical review. Pick one repository and check whether its claims match its evidence.
  • Connect a research partner. FAC has a community and questions. It needs a study-design collaborator.
  • Help shape a pilot. Portal, technical assistance network, or federated research records.

For the Roadmap facilitators, the asks map onto the seven breakout points and Tracks A through D. See the mid-level and deep views of each talking point for the track tags.

Contact: Shaun "Oden" Marshall, shaunmarshall.com/cv. Florida Armored Combat: flarmored.org.

PilotAccountable partner to identifyMeasure
Supported referralsReceiving program and named navigatorTime to a useful connection; referrals completed
Technical assistanceEngineering or validation teamExternal adoption; reproducible results; maintenance continuity
Reusable research recordsSource custodians and reviewersReview effort; missing evidence; reusable learning

Start with a bounded pilot, an accountable partner, and a measure of success. Preserve source records and limitations so later reviewers can assess what the pilot established.

Participant proposals for the Widener-led, NSF-funded convening. Project examples include documented results, work in development, and proposed pilots.
